reasons: The rule is a 'missing'-kind insert and the finding is properly framed as missing: the cited paragraph 20(i) is the final General Matters subsection, and nothing in the supplied text contradicts the stated absence of any insurance or certificate obligation.

The redline is additive only — it leaves p0147 untouched and appends a new 20(j) — which is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where Customer Data is handled, workers' comp as required by law, certificates on request).

The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required [Playbook] prefix, states what changed and why (on-premises installation and data conversion), and offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback as the rule contemplates.

Deterministic checks confirm the insertion applies and an insurance obligation is now present; the rationale's reference to walk-away territory is consistent with the rule's walk-away text (no insurance for a vendor working on our premises / touching our data).
